content: {"summary":"Internal name resolution failure in Feb 2025 was caused by CPU‑starved CoreDNS pods (only two replicas) that could not handle the query load, leading to time‑outs across auth, catalog and orders services.","likely_cause":"CoreDNS pods were under‑provisioned (CPU‑saturated with only 2 replicas), causing name‑resolution timeouts.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"CoreDNS pods hit CPU ceiling with only two replicas, causing timeouts","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#1"],"quote":"2 replicas, each flat against its CPU ceiling"},{"text":"CPU starvation of CoreDNS caused loss of name resolution in all namespaces","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#2"],"quote":"Starve those CoreDNS pods of CPU and every namespace loses name resolution together"},{"text":"Scaling CoreDNS to four replicas restored lookups","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#1"],"quote":"scaled coredns to 4 replicas both new pods Ready and answering"}],"next_checks":["Implement autoscaling for CoreDNS based on CPU/request latency","Add alert on CoreDNS request p99 latency","Review typical query volume and adjust replica count accordingly"]}
